dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: The sense of crisis people have at the Palais Mermonia is just... hard to assess.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They do seem quite busy.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: And there's the rub.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: We should ask ourselves this honestly — if we did work at normal efficiency and with the usual workload at Maison Gestion, how much would we be able to do?

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: I never thought about any of this when I was with the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. Only when I grew older and transferred to the Maison Gestion did I have more and more questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Patrol...

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: The Patrol's membership is highly streamlined, picking only the best of the best, regardless of any member's past.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: Even if they are the children of criminals and thus of ill repute, they can join the Patrol so long as they have the ability.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: This sounds funny, but the Patrol is the least mechanized section of the Gardes.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: If you asked the present Captain, Chevreuse, about that, she'd say, "Gardemeks will only block our bullets!"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you referring to the "prophecy"?

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: Ah. Are you concerned about it as well?

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: Good. Then you've got a better nose for danger than many people here in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: There is no point discussing the veracity of such a thing, because before a crisis comes, no one can truly use accurate evidence to convince another.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: But if we don't consider it at all... Some might call it optimism. Others would call it folly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: See you. Wish us all luck.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you referring to the "prophecy"?

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: The prophecy is the biggest crisis Fontaine has faced so far. But I have other things to worry about as well.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: And even today some are discussing whether the prophecy was real or not. They just can't see what's really important.

dialogues.speaker: Riqueti
dialogues.text: We can't ignore all our other problems simply because we survived a major crisis. Assuming that life will be easy from now on is... well, it's either optimism or ignorance.
